svg.title: Two agents on gitta's own code. gitta warns the second agent, stops the failing git merge, and lets it through once the code fits.

text.tspan: gitta init --gate "python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/aidev-replay -q"
gitta is set up in gitta.
It watches the 2 agent worktrees ci-level, ci99. Every worktree an agent tool creates from
now on is picked up on its own.
# agent 1 (ci-level) makes z keyword only in wilson
# agent 2 (ci99) writes new code that calls it the old way
# gitta tells agent 2, inside its own session
Gitta:
agent ci-level changed `wilson`, which your new code in bench/aidev-replay/analyze.py
calls. Check that your code still fits. Their version: bench/aidev-replay/analyze.py:23: def
wilson(k, n, *, z=1.96):
git merge --no-edit ci-level
Updating b8cb38d..d0b971a
Fast-forward
bench/aidev-replay/analyze.py | 2 +-
bench/aidev-replay/test_wilson.py | 9 +++++++++
2 files changed, 10 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
create mode 100644 bench/aidev-replay/test_wilson.py
git merge --no-edit ci99
Auto-merging bench/aidev-replay/analyze.py
gitta:
tests fail on main with ci99 (test_ci99.T.test_wider); main unchanged, merge
cancelled (ignore git's note). Fix it and merge again.
TypeError: wilson() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given
Now on main: bench/aidev-replay/analyze.py:23: def wilson(k, n, *, z=1.96):
Not committing merge; use 'git commit' to complete the merge.
# agent 2 fixes its call
git merge --no-edit ci99
Auto-merging bench/aidev-replay/analyze.py
Merge made by the 'ort' strategy.
bench/aidev-replay/analyze.py | 5 +++++
bench/aidev-replay/test_ci99.py | 9 +++++++++
2 files changed, 14 insertions(+)
create mode 100644 bench/aidev-replay/test_ci99.py
gitta watch --once
Today gitta checked 3 changes, caught 1 clash before main, and merged 2 pieces of work.
gitta is set up. It checks every agent worktree in this repository against main.
gitta found the agent worktree ci-level and checks its changes from now on.
gitta found the agent worktree ci99 and checks its changes from now on.
ci-level edited analyze.py, test_wilson.py. Nothing else is affected.
! ci99's new code in bench/aidev-replay/analyze.py calls wilson, which ci-level
changed. gitta told ci99 before anything reached main.
+ Tests passed on main combined with ci-level's changes. ci-level was merged into
main with git merge.
gitta stopped the git merge: tests fail on main combined with ci99
(test_ci99.T.test_wider).
gitta cancelled the stopped merge attempt, so main is as it was.
ci99's new code in bench/aidev-replay/analyze.py calls wilson, which changed on
main. The tests at merge time decide.
+ ci99 changed analyze.py to fit ci-level's change to wilson. That clash is solved.
+ Tests passed on main combined with ci99's changes. ci99 was merged into main with
git merge.
